chunks: And in the narration of ʿAmr ibn Jumayʿ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:
Defrauding the trusting party is riba.

key_terms.رِبًا: usury; illicit excess treated here as a grave unlawful financial wrong
key_terms.غَبْنُ: fraudulent overcharging or unfair disadvantage in a transaction
key_terms.ٱلْمُسْتَرْسِلِ: the trusting, unsuspecting, or non-bargaining party in a sale

ai.seo_question: Is defrauding a trusting or unaware buyer considered riba in Islamic teachings?
ai.summary: This hadith condemns taking unfair advantage of a person who trusts the seller or lacks bargaining awareness. It frames such exploitative overcharging as riba, highlighting the grave moral and legal seriousness of dishonest gain in transactions.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3983 - In a narration from Amr ibn Jameei, from Abu Abdullah (as), he said:
"Defrauding the one who entrusts you is usury."
